questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

This is the book whom I wanted to buy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3) **i.e. **'whom I'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pronoun "**whom**" is incorrectly used in this sentence.
 
• "**Whom**" is used as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• In this sentence, "**that**" should be used as it introduces a defining clause describing "**the book.**"
 
• Thus, the correct sentence should be *"This is the book **that **I wanted to buy."*

Therefore, the correct answer is **'whom I'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option (1) 'the book': **This is a correct phrase and there is no grammatical error in it. It correctly identifies the noun being discussed.
 
• **Option (2) 'wanted to buy.':** This phrase is also grammatically correct and maintains the intended meaning of the sentence, expressing the desire to purchase.
 
• **Option (4) 'This is': **This phrase is correct as it properly introduces the sentence and gives context, indicating what is being referenced.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Everyone should respect those parents, teachers, and elders.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. respect those has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"respect those"** is incorrect because it implies that "**those**" is necessary, which it is not.
 
• In context, the sentence should simply be "Everyone should respect parents, teachers, and elders"** without the word "those."**
 
• Using "**those**" unnecessarily complicates the sentence and makes it awkward.
 
• Correcting the sentence improves its readability and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: *Everyone should respect parents, teachers, and elders*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("and elders.")** is correct as it is appropriately punctuated and completes the list.
 
• **Option 2 ("parents, teachers,") **is correct as it appropriately lists the nouns in the series.
 
• **Option 4 ("Everyone should,")** is correct as the introductory phrase of the sentence.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. 

They were / married happily / before she / quit her job.

A B C D
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'B' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the phrase 'married happily' is incorrect.
 
• The correct form should be 'happily married', as the adverb should come before the adjective.
 
• Adverbs generally modify adjectives, verbs, or other adverbs, and in this case, it should modify the adjective 'married'.
 
• Therefore,** 'happily married'** is the grammatically correct form.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *They were happily married before she quit her job*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 (D): 'quit her job' is correct as it properly indicates the action taken by 'she'.
 
• Option 3 (C): 'before she' is correct as it introduces the clause that follows.
 
• Option 4 (A): 'They were' is correct as it is the proper subject and verb agreement for a plural subject.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

By this time tomorrow, I _______ the work assigned to me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 3' i.e. will have done.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the future perfect tense, which indicates that an action will be completed before a specified time in the future.
 
• The structure of the future perfect tense is: **"will have" + past participle of the verb.**
 
• The past participle of "**do**" is "**done**."
 
• The phrase **"By this time tomorrow" **sets a future point by which the action will be completed, which aligns with the future perfect tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: will have done.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"will have did" is incorrect because "did" is the simple past form, not the past participle.
 
• **Option 2:** "will do" is the simple future tense, which does not indicate the completion of the action before a specified future time.
 
• **Option 4: "**will be done" is passive voice and does not fit the context where the subject "I" should be performing the action.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank. 

_________ that thought. It will be a great idea someday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1** i.e. **Hold onto.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence indicates that the thought should be kept or remembered because it may be useful in the future.
 
• The phrase **"Hold onto"** means to keep or maintain something, which fits the context of preserving a thought for future use.
 
• The other options do not fit the context as well:
 
 
• **"Hold to"** usually means to adhere to or follow a principle, which does not fit the context of keeping a thought.
 
• **"Hold on"** generally means to wait or to hang on, which is not appropriate here.
 
• **"Hold against"** means to have a grudge or resentment, which is not relevant in this context.
 
 
 
• Understanding the meaning of **"Hold onto"** in the context of the sentence helps to clarify that the idea should be preserved for potential future use.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Hold onto**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hold onto** (सहेजना) means to keep or maintain something.
 
• **Hold to** (पालन करना) means to adhere to or follow a principle.
 
• **Hold on** (रुको) means to wait or to hang on.
 
• **Hold against** (विरोध करना) means to have a grudge or resentment against someone.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, “Two and two make four.”

options.text: He says that two and two made four.
He said that two and two make four.
He says that two and two make four.
He said that two and two made four.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **He said that two and two make four.**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The sentence in the Direct Speech is a** universal truth or a general statement.**
 
• **Universal truths or general statements** remain** unchanged **in Indirect Speech.
 
• **Present tense **remains in the present tense to convey the general fact.

 
 

 **Direct Speech**
 **Indirect Speech**
 
 

 “Two and two make four.”
 two and two make four
 
 

 He said,
 He said that
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***He said that two and two make four**.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The award was presented to her by the director.

options.text: She presented the award to the director.
The award presented to her by the director.
The director presented the award to her.
She was presenting the award to the director.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The director presented the award to her.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The **subject** of the **Active Voice** is changed into the **object** of the **Passive Voice**. Also, the **object** of the **Active Voice** is changed into the **subject** of the **Passive Voice**.
 
• The usage of a **helping verb** is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.
 
• The preposition **“by”** is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.
 
• The **sentence** provided in the question is in Passive Voice.
 
• To change the sentence to Active Voice, use the format: **Subject + Verb + Object.**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **The director presented the award to her.**

questions.question:
Select the option that arranges the given words to form a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence.

The students eagerly their awaited results.

options.text: The students their eagerly awaited results.
The awaited eagerly results their students.
Eagerly awaited the students their results.
The students eagerly awaited their results.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. The students eagerly awaited their results.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence needs to be arranged in a grammatically correct and meaningful way.
 
• In English, the subject typically comes first, followed by the verb, and then the object.
 
• The word "**eagerly**" is an adverb and should be placed before the verb "awaited" to describe how the action was performed.
 
• The word "**their**" is a possessive pronoun and should be placed before "results" to show ownership.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *The students eagerly awaited their results*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2:** "The awaited eagerly results their students." - This option is completely jumbled and does not form a meaningful sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "Eagerly awaited the students their results." - The adverb "**eagerly**" is correctly placed, but the structure is incorrect because the subject should come first.

questions.question:

• The appropriate superlative form of "**challenging**" is "**most challenging**."
 
• Using **"most challenging"** correctly conveys that this task is the highest degree of challenge compared to all others encountered.
